## Dry-channel positivity inside the implicit solve {#sec-ch08-vic}

<!-- PROVENANCE

sources: OUTLINE.md 8.10

### Summary

The implicit correction of the time-integration chapter solves a column and hands back a mass change that no face
limiter has seen. That change can exceed what a cell holds. This section is the guard on that path.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Clip each implicit dry-gas face transfer to what its donor still holds, and record that a donor was emptied.

**Data.** In: the column state, the explicit increment, the requested transfers. Out: clipped transfers, paired cell increments, a flag.

**Placement.** Pass 3a of the implicit redistribution, inside the vertical implicit solve of every stage.

**Activation.** With `integration/implicit-scheme`; no switch of its own.

**Guarantee / limits.** No additional overdraw and exact column mass; a state already negative before the transfer is not repaired.

**Evidence.** `test_backward_substitution.<b>` ($10^{-12}$); `[C8]` of this chapter's check is a counter-example only.
:::

### Derivation

The explicit limiter does not constrain the later implicit correction. The implicit path
therefore converts its column correction into face transfers and limits each constituent's
transfer by the donor's remaining availability. Each limited transfer is subtracted from
one cell and added to its neighbour, conserving column mass.

`[C8]` in `positivity_check.py` is only a synthetic counterexample: an arbitrary conservative redistribution can
undo explicit positivity, and a subsequent pointwise floor would create mass. It is not a
port of the implicit solver and does not measure the implemented availability clamp.

### Numerical method

The actual dry clamp is pass 3a of
{{< code src/implicit/vic_redistribute_impl.h vic_constituent_column >}}.
It clips the signed dry transfer to the interval from minus the upper donor's availability
to the lower donor's running availability. The paired increments preserve mass; the clamp
changes the requested transfer, rather than flooring the final density.

When a dry transfer is clipped, `MASS(IPR, donor)` is set to 1. The maximum copied into
`_dry_clamp_step` by {{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}
is therefore a binary flag, not a mass magnitude. The redo detector tests whether it is
positive ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::vic_dry_clamp_hit >}}).
The accessor and reset are {{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.hpp ImplicitHydroImpl::dry_clamp_step >}}
and {{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.hpp ImplicitHydroImpl::reset_dry_clamp_step >}}.

**Why a clamp on the transfer.** Three facts of the code.

1. The transfer through a face is clipped to the interval from minus the upper donor's availability to the lower
   donor's running availability ({{< code src/implicit/vic_redistribute_impl.h vic_constituent_column >}}). So neither
   donor is drawn below zero by this face.
2. The clipped transfer is subtracted from one cell and added to its neighbour, so the column mass is unchanged by the
   clamp. The requested transfer changes, not the final density.
3. A clip sets `MASS(IPR, donor)` to 1, and the step buffer keeps the maximum, so the record is a flag and not a mass
   ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}).

: Code map of the implicit dry-channel clamp. {#tbl-ch08-vic-code}

**How to use it.** The clamp is part of the implicit scheme and has no key of its own; it runs whenever the
scheme is selected ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=1 >}}):

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `integration`[^rg-1f094ab5857c], `implicit-scheme`[^rg-a333df308337].
```yaml
integration:
  implicit-scheme: 1   # vic-partial; 9 is vic-full, 0 none
```

The value is an integer (`as<int>`, {{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=2 >}}):
1 selects the partial and 9 the full VIC[^rg-bc116a6d3149], and 0 is the explicit scheme. Any other value fails when the scheme is named
(`type`), and a map such as `{type: vic}` does not parse as an integer.

The clip is these lines of pass 3a ({{< code src/implicit/vic_redistribute_impl.h vic_constituent_column >}}):

```cpp
    T Mf = MASS(IVX + dir, i + 1);
    T q = Mf > 0 ? Mf * dryfrac : Mf * dryfrac_up;
    if (q > avail) {
      q = avail;
      MASS(IPR, i) = 1;
    }
    if (q < -avail_up) {
      q = -avail_up;
      MASS(IPR, i + 1) = 1;
    }
```

`q` is the dry transfer through the face above cell `i`, `avail` and `avail_up` the two donors' availabilities,
and `MASS(IPR, ...)` the flag the redo detector reads.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- Availability limiting prevents additional overdraw; it does not repair a state already negative before the implicit transfer.
:::

1. **Not ported.** This chapter's checks cover the explicit limiter and the floors. The implicit clamp
   is inside a solve this chapter does not reproduce, so its behaviour is recorded from the code.
2. **A flag, not a budget.** The buffer records whether a dry donor was emptied by clipping a transfer; it does not measure transferred mass.
